How to read this page

This page is for collaborators who will use the numbers in a paper. The code can be skipped. Each section states the threshold and the result.

All tables and figures are in results_bundle.zip. Download that file to place the results in a paper. The same files also sit in results/ and are linked one by one below. For a paper layout, use the PDF files. The PNG files are 140 dpi previews for this page; do not use a screenshot of the page as the final figure.

To redraw one chart: open the ZIP, open the workbook named in the plot guide, choose the sheet, and copy the columns listed there. For GO or KEGG, go_up and kegg_up are genes higher in the group before _vs_, and go_down and kegg_down are genes higher in the group after _vs_. Plot Description against FoldEnrichment or NES, with one row as one bar. For a volcano, plot log2FoldChange against neg_log10_padj_for_plot. For one gene, use results/2_normalized_expression.xlsx; each point is one sample.

Files in results/ are numbered in the order of the analysis. expression_based means the score was inferred from each sample’s expression. differential_based means the score was inferred from the unshrunk Wald statistic. A positive differential score means higher activity in the group named before _vs_ in the file name.

  1. PCA
  2. Differential expression
  3. Enrichment
  4. PROGENy
  5. Transcription factors
  6. CytoSig
  7. Counts and abundances, for looking up a gene

In the differential plots, red means higher in Treatment than in Control. Blue means the opposite. One PCA is coloured by group and one by sex. The male-only and female-only PCAs are coloured by group. Heatmap colours are relative scores across samples, as shown in each legend.

Thresholds used throughout:

  • Differential genes: Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted P < 0.05. No minimum fold change.
  • Low-count genes: a gene is kept only if at least as many samples as the smallest group have a count of 10 or more. The number remaining is given with the differential-expression results.
  • Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA): adjusted P < 0.05.
  • PROGENy, transcription-factor and CytoSig activity: P < 0.05.

Samples and alignment

Reads were pseudoaligned with kallisto and then summarised to protein-coding genes. The alignment rate is the percentage of reads that matched a transcript. A higher rate means more of that sample could be used.

Show code 
tx2gene <- read_tsv(t2g_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::filter(tx_type == "protein_coding", gene_type == "protein_coding") %>%
  dplyr::distinct(tx_id, gene_id, gene_symbol)

sample_annot <- read_tsv(file.path(repo_root, "sample_annotation.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::filter(batch == batch_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = relevel(factor(group), ref = "Control"))

info_files <- file.path(repo_root, "kallisto_quant", batch_id, sample_annot$sample_id, "run_info.json")
alignment <- purrr::map_dfr(info_files, read_kallisto_run_info)
sample_annot <- bind_cols(sample_annot, alignment) %>%
  as.data.frame()
rownames(sample_annot) <- sample_annot$sample_id

abundance_files <- file.path(repo_root, "kallisto_quant", batch_id, sample_annot$sample_id, "abundance.tsv")
names(abundance_files) <- sample_annot$sample_id
stopifnot(all(file.exists(abundance_files)))

txi <- tximport(
  abundance_files,
  type = "kallisto",
  tx2gene = tx2gene[, c("tx_id", "gene_id")],
  ignoreTxVersion = TRUE,
  countsFromAbundance = "no"
)

Show code 
t2g_all <- read_tsv(t2g_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
pc_tx <- unique(t2g_all$tx_id[t2g_all$tx_type == "protein_coding" & t2g_all$gene_type == "protein_coding"])
qc_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(sample_annot)), function(i) {
  id <- sample_annot$sample_id[[i]]
  ab <- read_tsv(file.path(repo_root, "kallisto_quant", batch_id, id, "abundance.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  id_nov <- sub("\\..*$", "", ab$target_id)
  total_est <- sum(ab$est_counts, na.rm = TRUE)
  pc_est <- sum(ab$est_counts[id_nov %in% pc_tx], na.rm = TRUE)
  excluded <- id %in% samples_excluded
  tibble::tibble(
    sample_id = id,
    group = as.character(sample_annot$group[[i]]),
    treatment_definition = "pending experimental annotation",
    n_processed = sample_annot$n_processed[[i]],
    pseudoaligned_percent = sample_annot$p_pseudoaligned[[i]],
    protein_coding_estimated_counts = pc_est,
    total_estimated_counts = total_est,
    protein_coding_fraction = pc_est / total_est,
    fraction_numerator = "sum of estimated counts for protein-coding transcripts",
    fraction_denominator = "sum of estimated counts for all transcripts in the kallisto abundance file",
    included = !excluded,
    exclusion_reason = if (!excluded) {
      ""
    } else if (exists("exclusion_reasons") && id %in% names(exclusion_reasons)) {
      unname(exclusion_reasons[[id]])
    } else {
      "removed before differential analysis"
    }
  )
})

Do the samples separate?

Principal component analysis (PCA) uses blind variance-stabilised counts and the 500 genes with the largest variance, as implemented in DESeq2. The first two plots use one PCA of every analysed sample: the same coordinates are coloured by group and then by sex. Male samples and female samples are then analysed in separate PCAs and coloured by group. Samples that sit close together have more similar expression among the genes used for that plot. Group separation does not have to fall on PC1.

Show code 
figure_paths <- character()
group_colors <- pca_group_colors
dds <- make_dds_from_counts(txi, sample_annot, design = dds_design)
smallest_group <- min(table(sample_annot$group))
dds <- filter_low_count_genes(dds, sample_annot)
vsd_pca <- DESeq2::vst(dds, blind = TRUE)
pca_all <- ntop_pca_data(vsd_pca, ntop = 500)
readr::write_tsv(pca_all$scores, "results/1_PCA_scores.tsv")
group_title <- if (length(samples_excluded) > 0) {
  "After removal, coloured by group"
} else if (isTRUE(adjust_sex)) {
  "All samples, coloured by group"
} else {
  NULL
}
pca_group <- save_pca_plot(
  pca_all$scores, pca_all$percent, "results/1_PCA.pdf",
  color_by = "group", title = group_title,
  show_legend = if (isTRUE(adjust_sex)) TRUE else NULL
)
figure_paths <- c(figure_paths, pca_group$png)
if (isTRUE(adjust_sex)) {
  sex_title <- if (length(samples_excluded) > 0) "After removal, coloured by sex" else "All samples, coloured by sex"
  pca_sex <- save_pca_plot(
    pca_all$scores, pca_all$percent, "results/1_PCA_by_sex.pdf",
    color_by = "sex", title = sex_title, show_legend = TRUE
  )
  figure_paths <- c(figure_paths, pca_sex$png)
  for (sex_level in c("male", "female")) {
    vsd_sex <- vsd_pca[, SummarizedExperiment::colData(vsd_pca)$sex == sex_level]
    pca_one <- ntop_pca_data(vsd_sex, ntop = 500)
    score_path <- sprintf("results/1_PCA_%s_scores.tsv", sex_level)
    pdf_path <- sprintf("results/1_PCA_%s.pdf", sex_level)
    readr::write_tsv(pca_one$scores, score_path)
    plotted <- save_pca_plot(
      pca_one$scores, pca_one$percent, pdf_path,
      color_by = "group",
      title = sprintf("%s samples, coloured by group", tools::toTitleCase(sex_level)),
      show_legend = TRUE
    )
    figure_paths <- c(figure_paths, plotted$png)
    if (sex_level == "male") pca_male <- plotted else pca_female <- plotted
  }
}

In the PCA of every analysed sample, PC1 explains 19% of the between-sample variation and PC2 explains 16%. The group-coloured and sex-coloured plots use these coordinates. In the male samples, PC1 explains 31% and PC2 explains 24%. In the female samples, PC1 explains 37% and PC2 explains 22%.

Differential genes

DESeq2 tests, for each gene, whether the difference between groups is larger than expected from the sampling noise. A gene is kept when at least as many samples as the smallest group have a count of 10 or more. Those genes are the ones used downstream. Fold changes are shrunk so that low-count genes are not given unrealistically large fold changes. The shrinkage method used for each comparison is stated in Methods.

Sex is a covariate in the model. The comparison is the group difference after adjustment for sex. A positive log2 fold change still means higher in the group named before _vs_.

A gene is reported as differential only when its Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted P is below 0.05. There is no extra fold-change cutoff. The counts below are the ones to use in the paper. The full table is results/2_DEGs_<comparison>.xlsx (sheets sig_up, sig_down, sig, clean and full). For a volcano, use gene_symbol, log2FoldChange and neg_log10_padj_for_plot. Significance stays padj < 0.05.

Show code 
dds <- DESeq(dds)

shrink_used <- character()
degs <- purrr::imap(contrasts, function(contrast, contrast_name) {
  shrunk <- shrink_contrast(dds, contrast, alpha = alpha)
  shrink_used[[contrast_name]] <<- attr(shrunk, "lfc_shrink")
  tidy_degs(shrunk, tx2gene, alpha = alpha)
})
purrr::iwalk(degs, function(result, contrast_name) {
  note <- tibble::tibble(
    column = c("log2FoldChange", "stat", "padj", "neg_log10_padj_for_plot", "padj_underflow"),
    meaning = c(
      "shrunk log2 fold change",
      "unshrunk Wald statistic",
      "Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted P. This is the value used to call significance at 0.05. Do not replace a stored 0.",
      "Finite -log10 value for plotting only. When padj underflowed to 0, this uses the smallest positive padj in the same table. It is not a new P value and is not the CytoSig permutation cap.",
      "TRUE when the stored padj is 0 because of DESeq2 numerical underflow."
    )
  )
  write_result_xlsx(c(result[c("full", "clean", "sig", "sig_up", "sig_down")], list(column_note = note)),
                    file.path("results", paste0("2_DEGs_", contrast_name, ".xlsx")))
})
norm_counts <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)
log_norm <- log2(norm_counts + 1)
sym <- tx2gene %>% dplyr::distinct(gene_id, gene_symbol)
as_gene_table <- function(mat) {
  as.data.frame(mat) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
    dplyr::left_join(sym, by = "gene_id") %>%
    dplyr::relocate(gene_symbol, .after = gene_id)
}
write_result_xlsx(list(
  normalized_counts = as_gene_table(norm_counts),
  log2_normalized_plus1 = as_gene_table(log_norm),
  column_note = tibble::tibble(
    item = "use",
    value = "Use normalized_counts or log2_normalized_plus1 for one gene across samples. Do not plot raw estimated counts as expression. These values are not a complete solution for comparing different genes with each other."
  )
), "results/2_normalized_expression.xlsx")

Which genes changed?

In the volcano plot, the x-axis is the log2 fold change and the y-axis is the adjusted P value. Points higher up are more significant. Points further from the centre have a larger fold change. Grey points do not pass adjusted P < 0.05. The vertical line is at a fold change of zero because no fold-change cutoff was applied. At most 12 gene labels are drawn. The full table is the place to choose other genes.

A stored adjusted P of exactly 0 is numerical underflow from DESeq2, not a probability of zero and not the same thing as a CytoSig permutation P of 0. The column neg_log10_padj_for_plot places those rows at the smallest positive adjusted P in the same table. Significance remains the original padj < 0.05. padj_underflow marks the capped rows.

Show code 
figure_paths <- character()
purrr::iwalk(degs, function(result, contrast_name) {
  clean <- result$clean
  clean <- clean[!is.na(clean$padj) & !is.na(clean$log2FoldChange), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!"neg_log10_padj_for_plot" %in% names(clean)) clean <- add_de_plot_padj(clean)
  keyvals <- ifelse(
    clean$padj < alpha & clean$log2FoldChange > 0, "#B2182B",
    ifelse(clean$padj < alpha & clean$log2FoldChange < 0, "#2166AC", "grey60")
  )
  keyvals[is.na(keyvals)] <- "grey60"
  poles <- strsplit(contrast_name, "_vs_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  names(keyvals)[keyvals == "#B2182B"] <- paste("Higher in", gsub("_", " ", poles[[1]]))
  names(keyvals)[keyvals == "#2166AC"] <- paste("Higher in", gsub("_", " ", poles[[2]]))
  names(keyvals)[keyvals == "grey60"] <- "Non-sig"
  sig_lab <- clean[!is.na(clean$gene_symbol) & clean$gene_symbol != "" & clean$padj < alpha, , drop = FALSE]
  up_lab <- sig_lab[order(-sig_lab$log2FoldChange), , drop = FALSE]
  down_lab <- sig_lab[order(sig_lab$log2FoldChange), , drop = FALSE]
  select_lab <- unique(c(utils::head(up_lab$gene_symbol, 6), utils::head(down_lab$gene_symbol, 6)))
  clean$padj_draw <- ifelse(clean$padj_underflow %in% TRUE, 10^(-clean$neg_log10_padj_for_plot), clean$padj)
  x_max <- max(abs(clean$log2FoldChange), na.rm = TRUE)
  y_max <- max(clean$neg_log10_padj_for_plot, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(y_max)) y_max <- 1
  plot <- EnhancedVolcano(
    clean,
    lab = clean$gene_symbol,
    selectLab = select_lab,
    x = "log2FoldChange",
    y = "padj_draw",
    title = stringr::str_wrap(gsub("_", " ", contrast_name), 32),
    titleLabSize = 14,
    subtitle = NULL,
    caption = NULL,
    FCcutoff = 0,
    pCutoff = alpha,
    xlim = c(-x_max, x_max) * 1.15,
    ylim = c(0, y_max * 1.12),
    ylab = "-log10(adjusted P)",
    axisLabSize = 14,
    labSize = 3.5,
    legendPosition = "bottom",
    legendLabSize = 10,
    colCustom = keyvals,
    drawConnectors = TRUE,
    widthConnectors = 0.4,
    max.overlaps = 20
  )
  ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("2_volcano_", contrast_name, ".pdf")),
         plot, width = 7.2, height = 6.6)
  ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("2_volcano_", contrast_name, ".png")),
         plot, width = 7.2, height = 6.6, dpi = 140)
  figure_paths <<- c(figure_paths, file.path("results", paste0("2_volcano_", contrast_name, ".png")))
})

Which functions do those genes fall into?

Gene Ontology (GO) is a catalogue of gene functions. The Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) is a catalogue of known pathways. Both are run separately on genes that went up and on genes that went down. A term is reported only when its Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted P is below 0.05. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) does not start from that gene list. It ranks every tested gene by the unshrunk Wald statistic, the same statistic used for the differential PROGENy, transcription-factor and CytoSig scores, and asks whether genes from one set gather at the top or the bottom. GO and KEGG, for both over-representation and GSEA, use this species’ own annotation. Hallmark GSEA uses MSigDB. CytoSig is a separate ridge regression and is described in its own section. The same adjusted P < 0.05 cutoff is used.

Each comparison has a workbook results/3_enrichment_<comparison>.xlsx. The plot guide below links the file for every comparison. Each sheet lists only terms with p.adjust < 0.05. An empty sheet means the test finished and no term passed. A bar chart uses Description against FoldEnrichment. For GSEA, plot Description against NES. leading_edge_symbols lists the gene symbols in the GSEA leading edge. A GO or KEGG term does not mean that pathway was measured directly. A disease or infection name in a KEGG term does not show that the disease or pathogen is present. The column_note sheet defines the columns.

Show code 
read_verified_sheet <- function(path, sheet) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(data.frame())
  sheets <- openxlsx::getSheetNames(path)
  if (!sheet %in% sheets) return(data.frame())
  df <- as.data.frame(openxlsx::read.xlsx(path, sheet))
  if (nrow(df) > 0 && "p.adjust" %in% names(df)) df$passes_fdr <- !is.na(df$p.adjust) & df$p.adjust < alpha
  df
}
if (isTRUE(reuse_verified)) {
  enrichment_results <- lapply(names(contrasts), function(contrast_name) {
    path <- file.path("results", paste0("3_enrichment_", contrast_name, ".xlsx"))
    list(
      go_up = read_verified_sheet(path, "go_up"),
      go_down = read_verified_sheet(path, "go_down"),
      kegg_up = read_verified_sheet(path, "kegg_up"),
      kegg_down = read_verified_sheet(path, "kegg_down"),
      gsea_hallmark = read_verified_sheet(path, "gsea_hallmark"),
      gsea_kegg = read_verified_sheet(path, "gsea_kegg"),
      gsea_gobp = read_verified_sheet(path, "gsea_gobp")
    )
  })
  names(enrichment_results) <- names(contrasts)
} else {
universe <- rownames(dds)
hallmark <- if (identical(species, "Mouse")) {
  msig_term2gene(msig_species, "MH", db_species = "MM")
} else {
  msig_term2gene(msig_species, "H")
}

enrichment_results <- purrr::imap(degs, function(result, contrast_name) {
  enrichment <- list(
    go_up = run_go(result$sig_up$gene_id, universe, orgdb, alpha),
    go_down = run_go(result$sig_down$gene_id, universe, orgdb, alpha),
    kegg_up = run_kegg(result$sig_up$gene_id, universe, orgdb, kegg_organism, alpha = alpha, msig_species = msig_species),
    kegg_down = run_kegg(result$sig_down$gene_id, universe, orgdb, kegg_organism, alpha = alpha, msig_species = msig_species),
    gsea_hallmark = {
      fit <- run_gsea_msig(result$ordered_logfc, hallmark, tx2gene)
      fit$resource <- if (identical(species, "Mouse")) "MSigDB_v2024.1.Mm" else "MSigDB_v2024.1.Hs"
      fit
    },
    gsea_kegg = run_gsea_kegg(result$ordered_logfc, orgdb, kegg_organism),
    gsea_gobp = run_gsea_go(result$ordered_logfc, orgdb, tx2gene)
  )
  enrichment <- lapply(enrichment, enrichment_for_plotting)
  sheets <- list()
  for (nm in names(enrichment)) {
    full <- enrichment[[nm]]
    sig <- if ("passes_fdr" %in% names(full)) full[full$passes_fdr %in% TRUE, , drop = FALSE] else full
    if ("neg_log10_padj" %in% names(sig)) sig$neg_log10_padj <- NULL
    sheets[[nm]] <- sig
  }
  sheets$column_note <- tibble::tibble(
    column = c("GeneRatio", "BgRatio", "Count", "FoldEnrichment", "NES", "p.adjust", "leading_edge_symbols", "resource", "analysis_status"),
    meaning = c(
      "genes in the term and in the tested list, over mapped genes in the tested list",
      "genes in the term and in the background, over mapped genes in the background; the background is the genes used for differential expression",
      "number of tested genes in the term",
      "how much more often the term appears in the tested list than in the background",
      "normalised enrichment score. A positive NES is enriched toward the group named before _vs_. It is the position of the gene set in the Wald ranking, not a direct activity measurement.",
      "Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted P. This is the value used to decide significance. These sheets contain only terms below 0.05; an empty sheet means none passed.",
      "gene symbols in the GSEA leading edge",
      "GeneOntology for GO, KEGG_online for KEGG, the MSigDB version for Hallmark, or MSigDB_KEGG_LEGACY if the KEGG download failed",
      "completed, or completed_fallback when online KEGG over-representation was replaced by MSigDB KEGG_LEGACY"
    )
  )
  write_result_xlsx(sheets, file.path("results", paste0("3_enrichment_", contrast_name, ".xlsx")))
  enrichment
})
dir.create("results/resources", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write_result_xlsx(list(msigdb = tibble::tibble(
  item = c("package", "species_argument", "hallmark_rows", "hallmark_resource", "go_kegg"),
  value = c(
    paste0("msigdbr ", as.character(utils::packageVersion("msigdbr"))),
    msig_species,
    as.character(nrow(hallmark)),
    if (identical(species, "Mouse")) "MSigDB_v2024.1.Mm collection MH" else "MSigDB_v2024.1.Hs collection H",
    if (identical(species, "Mouse")) {
      "GO biological process from org.Mm.eg.db; KEGG organism mmu"
    } else {
      "GO biological process from org.Hs.eg.db; KEGG organism hsa"
    }
  )
)), "results/resources/msigdb_manifest.xlsx")
}

Treatment vs Control (adjusted P < 0.05)

GO: 1 terms for genes that increased and 7 for genes that decreased. KEGG: 4 and 1. GSEA: 16 Hallmark, 28 KEGG and 378 GO biological process.

Leading Hallmark sets: HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION; HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS; HALLMARK_MYC_TARGETS_V1; HALLMARK_MYOGENESIS; HALLMARK_UV_RESPONSE_DN.

Leading KEGG terms among increased genes: Staphylococcus aureus infection - Mus musculus (house mouse); Proteoglycans in cancer - Mus musculus (house mouse); Phagocytosis - Mus musculus (house mouse); IgSF CAM signaling - Mus musculus (house mouse).

Leading KEGG terms among decreased genes: ECM-receptor interaction - Mus musculus (house mouse).

Show code 
figure_paths <- character()
direction_label <- function(group_name, kind = c("genes", "gsea")) {
  kind <- match.arg(kind)
  if (kind == "genes") paste("Genes higher in", group_name) else paste("Enriched toward", group_name)
}
purrr::iwalk(enrichment_results, function(enrichment, contrast_name) {
  poles <- strsplit(contrast_name, "_vs_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  up_name <- gsub("_", " ", poles[[1]])
  down_name <- gsub("_", " ", poles[[2]])
  go_up_label <- direction_label(up_name, "genes")
  go_down_label <- direction_label(down_name, "genes")
  gsea_pos_label <- direction_label(up_name, "gsea")
  gsea_neg_label <- direction_label(down_name, "gsea")
  go_fill <- c("#B2182B", "#2166AC")
  names(go_fill) <- c(go_up_label, go_down_label)
  gsea_fill <- c("#B2182B", "#2166AC")
  names(gsea_fill) <- c(gsea_pos_label, gsea_neg_label)
  hall <- enrichment$gsea_hallmark
  if ("passes_fdr" %in% names(hall)) hall <- hall[hall$passes_fdr %in% TRUE, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(hall) > 0 && "NES" %in% names(hall)) {
    hall <- hall[order(hall$p.adjust), , drop = FALSE]
    hall <- utils::head(hall, 15)
    hall$label <- gsub("^HALLMARK_", "", hall$Description)
    hall$label <- gsub("_", " ", hall$label)
    hall$change <- ifelse(hall$NES > 0, gsea_pos_label, gsea_neg_label)
    hall$change <- factor(hall$change, levels = c(gsea_pos_label, gsea_neg_label))
    p <- ggplot(hall, aes(stats::reorder(label, NES), NES, fill = change)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.75) + coord_flip(clip = "off") + theme_bw() +
      scale_fill_manual(values = gsea_fill, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
      theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11),
        plot.margin = margin(8, 14, 10, 8)
      ) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = "NES", title = stringr::str_wrap(paste("Lowest-FDR Hallmark sets:", gsub("_", " ", contrast_name)), 48))
    ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("3_gsea_hallmark_", contrast_name, ".pdf")), p, width = 9, height = max(5.5, 0.32 * nrow(hall) + 2))
    ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("3_gsea_hallmark_", contrast_name, ".png")), p, width = 9, height = max(5.5, 0.32 * nrow(hall) + 2), dpi = 140)
    figure_paths <<- c(figure_paths, file.path("results", paste0("3_gsea_hallmark_", contrast_name, ".png")))
  } else {
    unlink(file.path("results", paste0("3_gsea_hallmark_", contrast_name, c(".pdf", ".png"))))
  }
  go_pieces <- list()
  if (is.data.frame(enrichment$go_up) && nrow(enrichment$go_up) > 0) {
    go_pieces[[length(go_pieces) + 1]] <- enrichment$go_up %>% dplyr::mutate(direction = go_up_label)
  }
  if (is.data.frame(enrichment$go_down) && nrow(enrichment$go_down) > 0) {
    go_pieces[[length(go_pieces) + 1]] <- enrichment$go_down %>% dplyr::mutate(direction = go_down_label)
  }
  go <- if (length(go_pieces)) dplyr::bind_rows(go_pieces) else data.frame()
  if ("passes_fdr" %in% names(go)) go <- go[go$passes_fdr %in% TRUE, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(go) > 0 && "FoldEnrichment" %in% names(go)) {
    go <- go[order(go$p.adjust), , drop = FALSE]
    go <- utils::head(go, 15)
    go$direction <- factor(go$direction, levels = c(go_up_label, go_down_label))
    go$bar_label <- stringr::str_wrap(go$Description, 42)
    duplicated_label <- duplicated(go$bar_label) | duplicated(go$bar_label, fromLast = TRUE)
    go$bar_label[duplicated_label] <- paste0(go$bar_label[duplicated_label], "\n(", go$direction[duplicated_label], ")")
    go <- go[order(go$FoldEnrichment, go$bar_label), , drop = FALSE]
    go$bar_label <- factor(go$bar_label, levels = unique(go$bar_label))
    p <- ggplot(go, aes(bar_label, FoldEnrichment, fill = direction)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.72) + coord_flip(clip = "off") + theme_bw() +
      scale_fill_manual(values = go_fill, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
      theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 18, 12, 8)
      ) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = "Fold enrichment", title = stringr::str_wrap(paste("Lowest-FDR GO terms:", gsub("_", " ", contrast_name)), 48))
    go_height <- max(6.2, 0.42 * nrow(go) + 2.2)
    ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("3_go_", contrast_name, ".pdf")), p, width = 10, height = go_height)
    ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("3_go_", contrast_name, ".png")), p, width = 10, height = go_height, dpi = 140)
    figure_paths <<- c(figure_paths, file.path("results", paste0("3_go_", contrast_name, ".png")))
  }
})

Are signalling pathways more or less active?

PROGENy does not measure the pathway protein itself. It infers activity from the downstream genes that respond to that pathway, using each pathway’s weights and its top 500 responsive genes. The 14 pathways are fit together with a multivariate linear model (MLM), because they share responsive genes. There are two inferences. The expression-based heatmap uses each sample’s expression: each row is a sample and each column is a pathway, and colour is relative to the average of these samples. Heatmap colour is not a between-group test. The table is results/4_progeny_expression_based.xlsx, with the unscaled scores and the scaled scores used for the heatmap.

The differential lollipop uses the Wald statistic and the same multivariate model. A positive score means higher activity in the group named before _vs_. The figure is coloured at P < 0.05.

Show code

purrr::iwalk(degs, function(result, contrast_name) {
  if (isTRUE(reuse_verified)) {
    pathway <- as.data.frame(readxl::read_excel(file.path("results", paste0("4_progeny_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".xlsx")), "progeny"))
    tf <- as.data.frame(readxl::read_excel(file.path("results", paste0("5_tf_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".xlsx")), "transcription_factors"))
  } else {
  stats <- result$clean %>%
    dplyr::arrange(padj) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(gene_symbol), !duplicated(gene_symbol)) %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_symbol, stat) %>%
    column_to_rownames("gene_symbol")

  pathway <- decoupleR::run_mlm(
    stats, progeny_model,
    .source = "source", .target = "target", .mor = "weight", minsize = 5
  )
  tf <- decoupleR::run_ulm(
    stats, collectri,
    .source = "source", .target = "target", .mor = "mor", minsize = 5
  )
  pathway <- add_activity_fdr(pathway, alpha)
  tf <- add_activity_fdr(tf, alpha)
  activity_note_sheet <- tibble::tibble(
    column = c("score", "p_value", "direction"),
    meaning = c(
      "model score; positive means higher in the group named before _vs_",
      "P value",
      "higher_in_numerator is the group before _vs_; higher_in_denominator is the group after _vs_"
    )
  )
  write_result_xlsx(list(progeny = pathway, column_note = activity_note_sheet), file.path("results", paste0("4_progeny_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".xlsx")))
  write_result_xlsx(list(transcription_factors = tf, column_note = activity_note_sheet), file.path("results", paste0("5_tf_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".xlsx")))
  }

  contrast_title <- gsub("_", " ", contrast_name)
  progeny_plot <- plot_activity_lollipop(
    pathway, "source", "score", "p_value",
    paste("PROGENy pathway activity:", contrast_title)
  )
  ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("4_progeny_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".pdf")), progeny_plot, width = 6, height = 4.5)
  ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("4_progeny_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".png")), progeny_plot, width = 6, height = 4.5, dpi = 140)
  progeny_lollipop_paths <<- c(progeny_lollipop_paths, file.path("results", paste0("4_progeny_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".png")))
  tf_top <- tf %>%
    dplyr::mutate(direction = ifelse(score > 0, "up", "down")) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(direction) %>%
    dplyr::slice_min(p_value, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
  tf_plot <- plot_activity_lollipop(
    tf_top, "source", "score", "p_value",
    paste("Transcription factor activity:", contrast_title)
  )
  ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("5_tf_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".pdf")), tf_plot, width = 7.5, height = 4.5)
  ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("5_tf_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".png")), tf_plot, width = 7.5, height = 4.5, dpi = 140)
  tf_figure_paths <<- c(tf_figure_paths, file.path("results", paste0("5_tf_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".png")))
})

Which transcription factors may be driving the change?

Transcription-factor activity is inferred from the genes a factor regulates, not from the expression of the factor itself. CollecTRI keeps its own mode-of-regulation values, and each factor is fit separately with a univariate linear model (ULM). The heatmap shows the 30 factors with the largest variance of the unscaled scores; scores are scaled only for display. The full unscaled and scaled tables are in results/5_tf_expression_based.xlsx. The lollipop shows up to 10 factors with the smallest P on each side. A positive score means higher activity in the group named before _vs_. The figure uses P < 0.05.

Treatment vs Control

PROGENy pathways: 1 higher (JAK-STAT) and 0 lower (none) at P < 0.05.

Transcription factors: 18 higher (Myc, Foxj1, Nfatc3, E2f4, Zeb1) and 54 lower (Prox1, Pitx2, Hoxa5, Irx1, Erg) at P < 0.05.

Cytokine signalling

CytoSig infers cytokine signalling with a ridge regression against 43 cytokine response signatures. It is not the same test as the linear models used for PROGENy and transcription factors. The expression-based heatmap starts from the same variance-stabilised expression, then standardises each gene across samples before the regression. Per-sample P values describe the fit of that sample’s profile; they are not a test between biological groups. The differential result uses the same unshrunk Wald statistic as GSEA, PROGENy and the transcription-factor scores. A positive score means a stronger cytokine signal in the group named before _vs_. Reported significance uses P < 0.05. Tables are results/6_cytosig_expression_based.xlsx and results/6_cytosig_differential_based_<comparison>.xlsx (cytokine, score, p_value).

Mouse gene symbols were converted to human orthologues before CytoSig.

purrr::iwalk(degs, function(result, contrast_name) {
  wald_symbols <- to_cytosig_symbols(result$clean$gene_symbol, species)
  wald_tbl <- result$clean %>%
    dplyr::mutate(gene_symbol = wald_symbols) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(gene_symbol), gene_symbol != "", !is.na(stat), !duplicated(gene_symbol)) %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_symbol, stat)
  wald_path <- file.path("cytosig", paste0("cytosig_wald_", contrast_name, ".tsv"))
  readr::write_tsv(wald_tbl, wald_path)
  wald_prefix <- file.path("cytosig", paste0("output_cytosig_wald_", contrast_name))
  if (!isTRUE(reuse_verified)) run_cytosig(wald_path, wald_prefix)
  z <- read_cytosig_table(paste0(wald_prefix, ".Zscore"))
  p <- read_cytosig_table(paste0(wald_prefix, ".Pvalue"))
  cytosig_fc <- add_cytosig_p_display(add_activity_fdr(tibble::tibble(
    cytokine = rownames(z), score = z[, 1], p_value = p[rownames(z), 1]
  ), alpha))
  cytosig_fc$source <- cytosig_fc$cytokine
  write_result_xlsx(list(
    wald = cytosig_fc,
    column_note = tibble::tibble(
      column = c("score", "p_value", "p_value_display", "p_for_plot", "p_zero_capped", "neg_log10_p", "padj", "direction", "input"),
      meaning = c(
        "CytoSig ridge score. A positive score is a stronger signal in the group named before _vs_. Significance in this report uses the original p_value < 0.05.",
        "Original permutation P from CytoSig. This is the value used to call P < 0.05. A value of 0 means no more-extreme draw was seen in 1,000 permutations; it is not a literal probability of zero.",
        "Display text. Zero permutation P values are shown as <0.001, the resolution of 1,000 permutations. This is not a new P estimate.",
        "Numeric value for plotting only. When the original P is 0, this is 1/1001. It is not used to call significance.",
        "TRUE when the original permutation P was 0 and p_for_plot was capped.",
        "Minus log10 of p_for_plot, so a zero permutation P still has a finite plotting value. Not used to call significance.",
        "Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted P stored for reference. Activity calls in this report do not use padj.",
        "higher_in_numerator is the group before _vs_; higher_in_denominator is the group after _vs_.",
        "Unshrunk Wald statistic, the same ranking used for GSEA, PROGENy and transcription factors."
      )
    )
  ), file.path("results", paste0("6_cytosig_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".xlsx")))

  contrast_title <- gsub("_", " ", contrast_name)
  cytosig_plot <- plot_activity_lollipop(
    cytosig_fc, "cytokine", "score", "p_value",
    paste("Cytokine activity:", contrast_title)
  )
  ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("6_cytosig_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".pdf")), cytosig_plot, width = 12, height = 4.5)
  ggsave(file.path("results", paste0("6_cytosig_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".png")), cytosig_plot, width = 12, height = 4.5, dpi = 140)
  figure_paths <<- c(figure_paths, file.path("results", paste0("6_cytosig_differential_based_", contrast_name, ".png")))
})

Cytokines: 6 higher (IL22, EGF, IL12, IL17A, IL1A) and 9 lower (BMP4, TGFB3, IL13, LIF, NO) at P < 0.05.

Looking up one gene

results/7_raw_counts.tsv holds kallisto estimated counts summed to genes. Those values can be fractional and are not normalised expression, so they should not be plotted as a group comparison for a gene. results/2_normalized_expression.xlsx has DESeq2 normalised counts and log2(normalised count + 1) for the genes used in differential expression; use those for a one-gene plot, where each point is one sample. results/7_tpm.tsv and results/7_expression.xlsx keep the kallisto abundance table for reference. They are not the recommended way to compare how highly different genes are expressed in this 3’ dataset. The expression tables include genes that were summarised from the annotation, while the differential table includes only genes that passed the count filter and have a test result.

Show code 
gene_symbols <- tx2gene %>% dplyr::select(gene_id, gene_symbol) %>% dplyr::distinct()
counts_tbl <- as.data.frame(txi$counts) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_symbols, by = "gene_id") %>%
  dplyr::relocate(gene_symbol, .after = gene_id)
tpm_tbl <- as.data.frame(txi$abundance) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_symbols, by = "gene_id") %>%
  dplyr::relocate(gene_symbol, .after = gene_id)
write_result_xlsx(list(counts = counts_tbl, tpm = tpm_tbl), "results/7_expression.xlsx")
readr::write_tsv(counts_tbl, "results/7_raw_counts.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(tpm_tbl, "results/7_tpm.tsv")

Summary

Thresholds, the main counts, and a few enrichment terms are below. Numbers in bold are the ones to quote. Tables in results/ can be opened in Excel and plotted without rerunning the analysis. For an enrichment bar chart, plot Description against FoldEnrichment or NES. Significance is p.adjust.

Thresholds

  • Samples analysed: 12 samples.
  • Low-count filter: a gene is kept when at least 6 samples have a count of at least 10. 8671 genes remained.
  • Differential genes: Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted P < 0.05. No fold-change cutoff.
  • GO, KEGG and GSEA: Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted P < 0.05.
  • PROGENy, transcription factors and CytoSig: P < 0.05.
  • Model: group, with sex included as a covariate. Expression heatmaps show group and sex.
  • GSEA, and the differential PROGENy, transcription-factor and CytoSig scores, use the unshrunk Wald statistic. Expression heatmaps use each sample’s expression. A positive score means higher in the group named before _vs_. Heatmap colour is not a between-group test.

Differential genes

Treatment vs Control: 11 genes higher in Treatment and 33 genes higher in Control.

How to read the enrichment

GO and KEGG test upregulated genes and downregulated genes separately. A term on one of those sheets is enriched among those genes. It is not a measurement that the pathway protein is active or inhibited. GSEA ranks every tested gene by the Wald statistic. The sign of NES is the direction of that enrichment. A disease or infection name in a KEGG term does not show that the disease or pathogen is present. These results come from the same expression matrix. Agreement is an expression-level pattern, not independent validation or a demonstrated mechanism. A change in bulk immune signal can reflect cell composition, cell state, or both.

Make a figure from a table

If you want to draw a figure yourself, the files below contain the values used for the plots on this page. Open the file named in the table, use the columns listed there, and filter or sort as you like. For one gene, open results/2_normalized_expression.xlsx, sheet normalized_counts or log2_normalized_plus1. Each column is one sample, and each point is one sample. Do not plot results/7_raw_counts.tsv as a group comparison: those are kallisto estimated counts and can be fractional. For GO or KEGG, go_up and kegg_up are genes higher in the group before _vs_, and go_down and kegg_down are genes higher in the group after _vs_. Plot one row as one bar, Description against FoldEnrichment. Significance is p.adjust < 0.05. Check Count and geneID: several terms can be supported by the same single gene. For GSEA, plot NES. A positive NES is enriched toward the group before _vs_, and a negative NES toward the group after it. Significance is p.adjust < 0.05. For PROGENy, transcription factors and CytoSig, plot score. Colour or filter with p_value < 0.05. A positive score is higher in the group before _vs_. Heatmap colour is relative across samples, not a between-group test.

Methods

The sections below can be pasted into a paper. Versions are those used for this run. Citations follow the text.

RNA-seq data preprocessing

Single-end 3’ mRNA-seq reads were pseudoaligned with kallisto (v0.52.0) [1] to the mouse GRCm39 (Ensembl, July 2026) transcriptome. Quantification used –single-overhang and –fr-stranded. Transcript abundances were summarised to protein-coding genes with tximport (v1.34.0) [2]. Gene-level analysis used rounded kallisto estimated counts and did not apply a transcript-length offset.

Differential expression

Gene-level counts were analysed with DESeq2 (v1.46.0) [3]. The model contained sex and group. Sex was included as a covariate, and the reported comparison is the group difference after adjustment for sex. A gene was retained only when at least 6 samples, the size of the smallest group, had a count of 10 or more. After this filter, 8671 genes were used for downstream analysis. Log2 fold changes were shrunk with apeglm (v1.28.0) [4]. A gene was called differential at Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted P < 0.05, with no fold-change cutoff. A positive log2 fold change means higher in Treatment than in Control.

Sample relationships were shown by principal component analysis (PCA) in DESeq2 (v1.46.0) [3]. Blind variance-stabilised counts were used, retaining the 500 genes with the largest variance. All analysed samples were drawn from one PCA and coloured separately by group and by sex. Male samples and female samples were then analysed in separate PCAs and coloured by group.

Functional enrichment

Over-representation of Gene Ontology (GO) terms and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathways, and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), used clusterProfiler (v4.14.3) [6,7]. The background for over-representation was the set of genes used for differential expression. For GSEA, genes were ranked by the Wald statistic. Hallmark sets were the native mouse MSigDB v2024.1.Mm collection, queried with msigdbr (v10.0.2). GO over-representation tested biological process, cellular component and molecular function in org.Mm.eg.db (v3.20.0), with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment within each ontology. GO gene-set enrichment tested biological process only. KEGG pathways used organism mmu. Terms were retained at Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted P < 0.05 [8,9].

Pathway, transcription-factor and cytokine activity

Pathway activity was inferred with PROGENy weights for the top 500 responsive genes per pathway [12], using the multivariate linear model (MLM) in decoupleR (v2.12.0) [14]. Transcription-factor activity used CollecTRI and its own mode-of-regulation values [13], fit separately with the univariate linear model (ULM). The expression heatmap shows the 30 factors with the largest variance of the unscaled scores; scaling was used only for display. Sample-level scores used variance-stabilised counts summarised to gene symbols. Differential PROGENy, transcription-factor and cytokine scores used the unshrunk Wald statistic, the same statistic used to rank genes for GSEA. Cytokine signalling was inferred with CytoSig [15], a ridge regression with 1,000 permutations and penalty alpha 10,000. For the expression-based CytoSig scores, each gene in the variance-stabilised matrix was standardised across samples before the regression. PROGENy, transcription-factor and CytoSig activities were reported at P < 0.05. Mouse gene symbols were converted to human orthologues [16]. Analyses were run in R 4.4.3.

[1] Bray NL, Pimentel H, Melsted P, Pachter L. Near-optimal probabilistic RNA-seq quantification. Nat Biotechnol. 2016;34:525–527.

[2] Soneson C, Love MI, Robinson MD. Differential analyses for RNA-seq: transcript-level estimates improve gene-level inferences. F1000Res. 2015;4:1521.

[3] Love MI, Huber W, Anders S. Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2. Genome Biol. 2014;15:550.

[4] Zhu A, Ibrahim JG, Love MI. Heavy-tailed prior distributions for sequence count data: removing the noise and preserving large differences. Bioinformatics. 2019;35:2084–2092.

[5] Stephens M. False discovery rates: a new deal. Biostatistics. 2017;18:275–294.

[6] Wu T, Hu E, Xu S, et al. clusterProfiler 4.0: A universal enrichment tool for interpreting omics data. Innovation. 2021;2:100141.

[7] Yu G, Wang LG, Han Y, He QY. clusterProfiler: an R package for comparing biological themes among gene clusters. OMICS. 2012;16:284–287.

[8] Ashburner M, Ball CA, Blake JA, et al. Gene Ontology: tool for the unification of biology. Nat Genet. 2000;25:25–29.

[9] Kanehisa M, Goto S. KEGG: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes. Nucleic Acids Res. 2000;28:27–30.

[10] Subramanian A, Tamayo P, Mootha VK, et al. Gene set enrichment analysis: a knowledge-based approach for interpreting genome-wide expression profiles. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA. 2005;102:15545–15550.

[11] Liberzon A, Birger C, Thorvaldsdóttir H, Ghandi M, Mesirov JP, Tamayo P. The Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB) hallmark gene set collection. Cell Syst. 2015;1:417–425.

[13] Müller-Dott S, Tsirvouli E, Vazquez M, et al. Expanding the coverage of regulons from high-confidence prior knowledge for accurate estimation of transcription factor activities. Nucleic Acids Res. 2023;51(20):10934–10949. doi:10.1093/nar/gkad841.
